title: Chromatin Immunoprecipitation Protocol for Histone Modifications in Adipose Tissue
author: Cayir, Tannæs, et al.
materials: Human frozen SAT and OVAT samples

Here, we isolate chromatin and determine the fragment size.33.Purify the chromatin with MinElute PCR purification kit.34.Add 5 volumes (1025 μL) of binding buffer (PB) to the sample.a.Add 40 μL of 3 M NaAc (pH: 5.2).35.Add 700 μL of the sample in MinElute column.a.Centrifuge 1 min at 13,000 rpm.b.Remove flow through.36.Load the rest of the samples in the same column until loading all the samples.a.Centrifuge 1 min at 13,000 rpm.b.Remove flow through.37.Wash with 700 μL of PE buffer.a.Centrifuge 1 min at 13,000 rpm.b.Remove flow through.38.Put the samples in a new collection tube and centrifuge for 1 min at 13,000 rpm.39.Put MinElute column in 1.5 mL low-DNA binding tube.a.Add 10 μL TE (Tris-EDTA) Buffer (pH = 8.0).b.Incubate for 1 min at 37°C.c.Centrifuge 1 min at 13,000 rpm.40.Maintain the samples at 55°C for 5–10 min to allow ethanol evaporation beforehand.Note: To remove any residual alcohol from the reaction.41.Use Qubit dsDNA HS kit and determine the dsDNA concentration by Qubit fluorometer.a.Prepare the standards used in the calibration.b.Prepare working solution.c.Add 1 μL of DNA to working solution.d.Measure the concentration.42.Add 1 μL gel-pilot loading (5×, QIAGEN) dye + 5 μL of chromatin (200–250 ng in total).a.Run at 90–100 V (45–60 min).b.Analyze DNA in a 1.5% agarose gel with suitable size markers (1000 bp) to determine fragment size.Alternatives: 2100 Bioanalyzer system (Agilent, USA) is an alternative approach for the fragment size and distribution. Briefly, prepare the gel-dye mix by high sensitivity DNA dye with high sensitivity DNA gel matrix. Load 9 μL of the gel-dye mix in wells in high sensitivity DNA chip as indicated in the protocol. Load 5 μL of green- capped high sensitivity DNA marker into the wells marked with the ladder symbol. Load the 1 μL of ladder and the samples, put in vortex mixer and start the chip run.Alternatives: Nanodrop offers an alternative approach, consistently providing concentration measurements that are higher than those obtained with the Qubit due to a lack of sensitivity. Qubit provides high sensitivity, whilst Nanodrop provides purity measurements.
In this section, we perform library synthesis.

steps.title: Cut frozen adipose tissue
steps.instruction: Cut the frozen adipose tissue in a mortar using a pre‑chilled scalpel on dry ice.

steps.title: Isolate chromatin and sonicate
steps.instruction: Lyse cells, isolate nuclei, and shear chromatin to the desired fragment size.

substeps.instruction: Add protease inhibitor cocktail (PIC), sodium butyrate (NaBu), and PMSF to all buffers immediately before use; keep all buffers and samples on ice.
Add 5 mL cold cell lysis buffer containing PIC, NaBu, and PMSF to each tube (on ice).
Homogenize the tissue with an OMNI homogenizer using a Hard Tissue Omni Tip (blue): 3 × 10 s pulses with a 30‑s break on ice between pulses.
Incubate tubes on ice for 30 min, vortexing 10 s every 3 min.
Centrifuge at 2 870 g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant by inverting the tube (leave tube upside down on paper to avoid lipid contamination).
Add 1 mL cold cell lysis buffer with PIC, NaBu, and PMSF; vortex and centrifuge again at 2 870 g for 10 min at 4 °C to pellet nuclei.
Resuspend the nuclear pellet in 150 µL cold nucleus lysis buffer containing 1.0 % SDS, PIC, NaBu, and PMSF; transfer to a 1.5 mL sonication tube.
Vortex and incubate on ice for 2 h.
Add 150 µL cold nucleus lysis buffer **without** SDS (final SDS concentration 0.5 %; total volume 300 µL).

Shear chromatin using a Bioruptor UCD‑300 (Diagenode): High power, 30 s ON / 30 s OFF, 8 cycles per run, repeat 4 times (32 cycles total). After each cycle briefly vortex, spin, and incubate 2 min on ice.

steps.title: Post‑shearing chromatin processing
steps.instruction: Separate chromatin from debris and keep an aliquot for quality control.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the sheared samples at 10 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C.
Collect the transparent middle layer (chromatin) without disturbing the top blurry layer or the bottom debris layer; transfer to low‑binding 1.5 mL tubes.
Take 10 µL of the chromatin for downstream quality and quantity assessment.

steps.title: Purify and assess fragment size
steps.instruction: Purify chromatin with a MinElute PCR purification kit, quantify DNA, and evaluate fragment size.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 volumes (1 025 µL) of MinElute binding buffer (PB) to the chromatin sample.
Add 40 µL of 3 M sodium acetate (NaAc), pH 5.2.
Load 700 µL of the mixture onto a MinElute column; centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 rpm and discard flow‑through.
Repeat loading until the entire sample has passed through the column.
Wash the column with 700 µL PE buffer; centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 rpm and discard flow‑through.
Place the column in a new low‑binding tube; add 10 µL TE buffer (pH 8.0), incubate 1 min at 37 °C, then centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 rpm to elute DNA.
Incubate the eluate at 55 °C for 5–10 min to evaporate residual ethanol.
Quantify DNA using the Qubit dsDNA HS kit: prepare standards, make working solution, add 1 µL DNA to 199 µL working solution, measure fluorescence.
Prepare a gel‑loading mix: 1 µL 5× gel‑pilot loading dye (QIAGEN) + 5 µL purified chromatin (containing 200–250 ng total DNA).
Run on a 1.5 % agarose gel at 90–100 V for 45–60 min alongside a 1 kb DNA ladder; visualize to confirm fragment size (≈200–500 bp).
Optional: assess fragment size distribution with an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer (high‑sensitivity DNA chip) or a Nanodrop spectrophotometer (note: Nanodrop gives higher apparent concentrations).

steps.title: Purify ChIP DNA
steps.instruction: Purify immunoprecipitated (ChIP) and INPUT DNA using the MinElute kit and determine concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 volumes of MinElute binding buffer (PB) to each ChIP and INPUT sample.
Add 40 µL of 3 M NaAc (pH 5.2) to each sample.
Load 700 µL of each sample onto a MinElute column; centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 rpm, discard flow‑through, and repeat until all material is loaded.
Wash columns with 700 µL PE buffer; centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 rpm and discard flow‑through.
Elute DNA by adding 10 µL TE buffer (pH 8.0) to each column, incubate 1 min at 37 °C, then centrifuge 1 min at 13 000 rpm.
Measure DNA concentration with the Qubit fluorometer.
Expected concentrations: INPUT ≈ 6 ng/µL; ChIP ≈ 0.3–2 ng/µL (higher values may indicate non‑specific binding).

steps.title: Prepare sequencing library
steps.instruction: Construct sequencing libraries from 0.20 ng ChIP/INPUT DNA using the ThruPLEX DNA‑Seq kit.

substeps.instruction: Use the DNA Unique Dual Index Kit (Takara/AH Diagnostics) with 8‑nt index primers (IDT for Illumina TruSeq DNA).
Dilute the combined ChIP/INPUT DNA in TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 0.1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0) to a total input of 0.20 ng in a 10 µL reaction volume (kit recommends 50 pg–50 ng).
Perform the three library‑preparation steps (template preparation, library synthesis, library amplification) according to the ThruPLEX protocol.
Thermal cycler settings: heated lid 101–105 °C; ramp rate 3–5 °C/s.
Amplify the library for 15 PCR cycles (as recommended for H3K36me3, H3K4me3, H3K4me1, H3K27me3, H3K27ac).

steps.title: Clean up library with AMPure
steps.instruction: Remove fragments <100 bp using AMPure XP beads and assess library quality.

substeps.instruction: Add AMPure XP beads to the completed library according to the manufacturer’s protocol (catalog 000387v001) to retain fragments ≥100 bp.
Perform the bead‑based wash steps as described in the protocol.
Elute the purified library in the recommended buffer.
Evaluate library size distribution and concentration with an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer using the High‑Sensitivity DNA kit.
